title: Eval-awareness screen: the same 20 questions after 15 openings (5 test-like, each with a same-length real-use twin, plus free-form real use and test-as-topic), 323 prompts, plus a held-out check on 500 chat transcripts
procedure: This is a neuron SEARCH: no candidate is claimed in advance. The two listed neurons are named controls (below). Stage 1 (public data): one forward pass per prompt in requests/eval-awareness-screen-001/prompts.jsonl (323 prompts, at most 39 Marin tokens each; same row format as probes/capybara-v1, with token ids and scored positions). Capture silu(gate)*up for every neuron in all 64 layers at every token, as for capybara-v1. Score each neuron side on the question's own tokens (identical across openings; build.py checks): (a) twin difference = for each of the 20 questions, activation after each test opening T1-T5 minus after its same-length real-use twin (R5, R6, R7, R8, R4), averaged over the 5 pairs; (b) topic difference = mean after T1-T5 minus mean after M1/M2 (real use whose opening mentions tests). Also reported per side: each twin pair alone, test vs R1-R3, and the means on the 13 near-miss targets and 10 unrelated sentences. Per layer, 100 random neurons are scored the same way as the baseline. Stage 2 (private data, held out): sides that pass stage 1, plus 100 random same-layer sides, are run on the 500 chat transcripts of jjpn2/eval_awareness (Needham et al. 2025; gated, CC-BY-NC-SA). eval_transcripts.py prep renders each as plain User/Assistant text cut to 1,024 tokens; per side, record the mean activation over each transcript's tokens; eval_transcripts.py score gives AUROC eval vs real on all 500 and on single-turn transcripts only, Spearman with the annotators' eval probability, and Spearman with length. Transcripts and their activations stay private; only per-side scores are published.
prediction: Pre-registered 2026-11-18, before any run: (a) some sides pass stage 1, but most of them are also high on the near misses, i.e. they track tests as a topic, not this-text-is-a-test. (b) Few sides, possibly none, separate the transcripts on the single-turn subset with AUROC >= 0.6. (c) Control L32-N24138- (outcome of a test comes next) is high after M1/M2 and on near misses and fails the topic rule; control L32-N26288+ (question ends, answer next) rises after every opening, twins included, and fails the twin rule. If either control passes stage 1 in full, the screen is reading test topic or Q&A format, and the run is void.
pass_rule: Stage 1: a side passes if (1) its twin difference is positive for at least 16 of 20 questions (sign test, chance about 0.006), (2) its mean twin difference beats the 95th percentile of the 100 random same-layer sides, and (3) its topic difference is positive for at least 16 of 20 questions. Stage 2: a stage-1 side passes the held-out check if its single-turn AUROC is at least 0.6 and above the 95th percentile of the 100 random same-layer sides on the same transcripts. A side that passes both is a candidate for a normal hunt request with fresh prompts; it is not by itself an explanation.
refuted_if: No side passes both stages while the controls behave. That is a clean null and will be reported as one: it would mean this kind of eval awareness is not carried by single MLP neurons that this set can find, or that a base model does not represent it from pretraining. It would not show that Marin lacks it; it could live in attention, in a direction across neurons, or only show in longer agentic contexts.
compute: Stage 1: 323 forward passes, 7,894 tokens in total, dense capture like capybara-v1. Stage 2: 500 forward passes, 88,761 tokens in total, reading only the stage-1 sides plus 100 random sides per affected layer.
outputs: Stage 1: the dense activations (or per-side summaries) for the 323 prompts, published like capybara-v1. Stage 2: per side, AUROC (all, single-turn), Spearman with annotator probability and with length; no transcript text or per-token activations.
